Simple approach: leg is a path from hip to pedal; animate the hip position? Common trick: legs rotate around pedal pivot with opposite rotation so foot stays on pedal. E.g., leg group rotate around crank center with the crank, but the leg itself counter-rotates around pedal center. 

Simpler lazy approach: draw leg as a path and animate with animateTransform on a group rotated around crank center in sync with pedals, with the leg pivoted at the pedal. Let me do: crank group rotates around (300,390). Each leg is inside a pedal group... Actually a standard trick:

<g> <!-- crank: rotates -->
  <animateTransform rotate around crank center 360 dur 2s>
  <g transform="translate(0,-22)"> <!-- pedal position, top -->
    <g> <!-- leg, counter-rotated around pedal so it stays verticalish -->
      <animateTransform rotate 0 to -360 around (0,22) ... 
      <path hip to pedal foot>
    </g>
    <rect pedal/>
  </g>
</g>

The hip end will move around a circle, so the hip doesn't stay attached to body. To keep it simple, draw legs connecting body to pedals with a bent shape, letting the leg counter-rotate to stay roughly vertical. The hip end will describe a circle of radius 22 around the crank — a slight bobbing, acceptable in cartoon. Or simpler: legs just rotate with pedals, feet fixed at pedals; body stays still; legs stretch. Cartoon-ish is fine.

Simplest that looks decent: two legs, each a path from near the body to the pedal, grouped with each pedal in the rotating crank; add counter-rotation on the leg to keep it pointing up. The hip end will wobble slightly but the body can overlap, hiding the joint.
